dataset_family: Single-centre Italian TMS-EEG cohort (Ferreri/Rossini group; ethics Campus Bio-Medico University of Rome): 17 aMCI and 15 age- and gender-matched healthy controls
method_family: Navigated single-pulse TMS with 32-channel EEG co-registration (TMS-evoked potentials/GMFP, ERSP, intertrial coherence), with corticospinal RMT/MEP from the same stimulation
what_it_shows: Baseline cross-sectional comparison, 17 aMCI vs 15 matched controls. TMS-evoked EEG separates the groups modestly: GMFP lower at 45-50 ms (p = 0.045), a group x channel interaction with C3 post hoc p < 0.001, and lower alpha/beta/gamma ITC at a few channels. Resting motor threshold and MEP amplitude from the same stimulation do not separate them (p = 0.87, p = 0.11). TMS-evoked ERSP also shows no group effect (p = 0.78), and the group main effect on the cortical map is non-significant (p = 0.54).
why: PDF identity confirmed: the map entry, DOI 10.3389/fnagi.2021.737281, title and author list (Ferreri ... Rossini) match the P-522 block. Read to the References. The study shows an evoked-EEG measure separating aMCI from a matched non-impaired comparator where another neurophysiological index of the same stimulation does not. That is part of the statement only, for four reasons. (1) The EEG response is perturbation-evoked at rest, not task-evoked: participants only fixated a wall target to stay awake (p.3). The 'task-evoked electrophysiology' element is therefore met only by analogy. (2) RMT and MEP amplitude are corticospinal excitability indices produced by the same TMS pulse. They are not a macrostructural volume, a static structural index or an unloaded behavioural measure. The paper never presents them as the comparator of the EEG measures: they appear in Table 1 and one Results sentence. The pairing is the finder's, so the loaded-versus-static head-to-head the statement requires is not the study's own. (3) The EEG separation itself is partial. The group main effect on the cortical map is non-significant (p = 0.54). ERSP, also a TMS-evoked EEG measure, shows no group effect (p = 0.78; no interactions). The GMFP difference comes from sample-by-sample t-tests with no stated multiplicity correction. The ITC post hoc p-values are 0.03-0.048 at most channels. The internal dissociation the authors do draw (ITC impaired, ERSP preserved) is evoked EEG against evoked EEG, not loaded against static. (4) N = 32. MMSE differs by construction (29.7 vs 26.7). The authors call the results preliminary (p.10). The registry codes the design 'longitudinal', but the aMCI-vs-control contrast used here is the baseline cross-sectional comparison, which fits required_design. The RMT/MEP null is in the PDF (Table 1, Results p.4), not in the summary block. Independence: Italian single-centre sample, with no overlap in site, cohort or authors with P-651, P-661, P-662, P-665/P-687 or P-666, or with the other candidates (P-633, P-1163). The method family (TMS-EEG) is distinct from every supporter's, though broadly 'evoked EEG' like P-661 and P-662. Not a preprint (Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience 2021). supports_narrowed is n/a because the round-20 narrowed wording declares VF-25 not a convergence. For reference, P-522 does not fill the electrophysiology gap that wording names, because its non-separating measure is not a static measure.

quotes.quote: A total of 17 patients with MCI were recruited based on the diagnostic criteria for aMCI (Albert et al., 2011). The control group (CO) consisted of 15 age- and gender-matched healthy subjects.
To ensure wakefulness, subjects were required to ﬁxate a target over the wall.

Age, gender distribution, and education were comparable between the groups, whereas, as expected, aMCI showed the lower MMSE scores than controls (Table 1). RMT and MEPs amplitude were similar between the groups (Table 1).
In this time window, the analysis revealed a decreased GMFP amplitude at 45–50 ms post-TMS in the aMCI than controls (p = 0.045), a latency range corresponding to the N45 TEP (Tremblay et al., 2019).

Post hoc analyses indicated lower alpha ITC in the aMCI than controls in C3, FC5, F7, T7, P7 (p = 0.03), and FC1 (p = 0.04); lower beta ITC in C3, FC1, and FC5 (p = 0.048); and lower gamma ITC in FC1 (p = 0.003) (Figure 2B).
